title: A small country with a big planning question
annotation: The country is small, mountainous, and physically constrained, meaning that growth is not just a question of adding more people. It is a question of where those people can live, how they move, what infrastructure they rely on, and what land must remain protected.
secondaryAnnotation: Today, Andorra's built environment occupies only part of the country's total land area, while much of the surrounding landscape is limited by steep terrain, protected natural areas, or existing development patterns. As the population changes, Andorra cannot simply expand outward without tradeoffs.

title: Not all land is buildable land
annotation: Andorra's total land area tells only part of the story. Protected landscapes, steep terrain, and existing development dramatically reduce the amount of land that can realistically absorb future growth. The remaining buildable cells become some of the country's most consequential planning decisions.

title: Three future growth patterns, compared across time
annotation: You've seen how little of Andorra is actually available for development. The next question is what happens as population, development, and economic pressures evolve within those limits. The model explores several possible futures for Andorra through 2049.

title: Planning choices become real through everyday access
annotation: Growth becomes tangible through daily life: how easily people can reach schools, transit, services, jobs, and one another. As population patterns change, so do travel distances, infrastructure demand, and the accessibility of the places people depend on.

title: The future is a decision, not just a forecast
annotation: Every planning decision improves some outcomes while putting pressure on others. This final experience lets the user compare those tradeoffs directly: how policy choices change population distribution, land use, infrastructure demand, accessibility, environmental pressure, and social outcomes.
reflectionPrompt: Which future would you choose for Andorra, and why?
